text:
alyssa: Heads-up: follow-up from the 02:14 UTC LB/TLS incident. Root cause narrowed to accidental SNI fallback in routing policy causing cross-region traffic to hit incompatible certs -> handshake failures and retries. Need owners + deadlines for remediation and recurrence guardrails.

sam: saw the same pattern in metric spikes (handshakes up 8x, retries up 3x) — impact mostly east->eu. Quick question: do we want a targeted rollback or a code patch that disables fallback?

mario: patch to disable fallback is safer long-term. I can prepare a revert/guard PR that preserves telemetry and adds a feature-flag. Will do an RFC-style PR and request expedited review. ETA: PR opened by EOD 2026-06-04 PST, rollout tomorrow morning with canary.

jia: I'll own canary plan + predeploy validation. Proposal: lb-config-canary v2 with 0.5% traffic in eu and us-east, run synthetic SNI test matrix (normal, missing SNI, mangled hostname) for 24h before ramp. Add a predeploy CI job: `verify_sni_matrix.sh` and include `openssl` checks. ETA: config + playbook in 3 business days.

ops-lead: concrete action list: 1) mario: PR to disable fallback + tests + feature flag (due 2026-06-05). 2) jia: canary route + CI checks + playbook updates (due 2026-06-09). 3) sre-oncall: add detection alert + synthetic (due 2026-06-06). 4) alyssa: customer comms/impact verification (due 2026-06-07).

sre-oncall: adding temporary Pager when TLS handshake failures > 40 in 5m for cross-region hops and retry-rate > 200% baseline. I'll add dashboard tiles: `tls_handshake_failures`, `lb_retry_rate`, `cross_region_hops` and a combined composite alert.

mario: PR link (will post when ready). Quick note for reviewers: include an integration test scenario that spins up a VM that strips SNI to ensure we don't reintroduce fallback silently. Also adding `DEBUG_LB_HANDSHAKE` gated runtime flag.

alyssa: good — also require logging of the `server_name` in LB access logs (sanitized), and add a rate-limited debug dump for the handshake stacktrace (only when flag enabled). No cert/private material.

sam: suggest adding an automated rollback hook: if synthetic fails > 5% in 30m during rollout, auto-roll back config and notify oncall. This will reduce blast radius for config pushes.

jia: I can add circuit-breaker + auto-rollback in canary orchestration. Proposed policy: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks at each step. Fail criteria: synthetic SNI failure or TLS handshake alerts.

ops-lead: please add the runbook steps to `runbooks/lb-tls-issues.md` and include exact kubectl/infra commands to abort and rollback. We'll require a sign-off checklist before any full roll.

mario: PR now: https://git.redwood/s/repo/pulls/1472 (WIP) includes tests + integration harness. Tagging @jia @ops-lead for review.

sre-oncall: synthetic ticket created: /observability/synthetics/sni-crossregion-check every 10m, groups: sni, cross-region, lb. Alert on >2 failures in 6 checks. Dashboard ETA: 2026-06-06.

incident-bot: postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/pm/2026-06-lb-tls-sni-2. Severity P2.

alyssa: recurrence note: this shares symptoms with Q1 sni incidents; add a "recurring incident class" section in the PM listing prior incidents, root-cause variants, and guardrails (canaries, feature-flags, synthetic coverage). Also add retrospective action to review all LB routing heuristics that touch SNI.

ops-lead: owners and dates repeated here for tracking: mario (disable fallback PR) due 2026-06-05, jia (canary + playbook) due 2026-06-09, sre-oncall (synthetic + alert) due 2026-06-06, alyssa (customer impact verification + comms) due 2026-06-07. We'll reconvene 2026-06-06 18:00 UTC for status.

jia: scheduling invite and adding agenda: PR review, canary config, rollback automation, synthetic validation.

mario: once PR merges I'll push canary commit and add step-by-step verification commands in PR body. Example verify command for SNI test:`./infra/tools/verify_sni.sh lb.redwood.test 10.0.0.5`

alyssa: thanks all. tagging this as canonical follow-up thread. If any ETA slips, escalate to ops-lead so we can prioritize. :thumbsup:
